summary.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還, whose earliest supported sense is “return; go back.” Later forms of 還 combine 辵, associated with movement, and 瞏, identified as a sound element. Modern 还 also means “still” and “yet,” but the sources do not establish how those senses relate to “return.”

formation.text: The later construction of 還 is phonosemantic: 辵 contributes a movement-related meaning, while 瞏 is identified as the sound element. A separate analysis proposes that 瞏’s sense “round jade disc” also contributes meaning; the received analysis assigns it only a phonetic role. Early forms are described with different component analyses, and their connection to this later construction is unclear.

components.text: In 还, 辶 is the conventional side form of 辵. 辵 is identified as movement-related in later forms of 還, but that analysis does not apply to every reported early form.

不 is visible in modern 还, whose recorded structure is ⿺辶不. Its appearance does not establish a meaning or sound role in the older 還 construction. A separate dictionary entry records a 不-associated graph 还 but does not connect it to this variant.

In later forms of 還, 瞏 is identified as a sound element. One analysis also proposes a meaning contribution from its “round jade disc” sense, while the received analysis assigns it only a phonetic role.

sound_limitation.text: No directly comparable historical reconstruction for 瞏 is supplied alongside one for 還, so the sound match cannot be assessed from the available pronunciation records.

history.text: Early forms of 還 are described as having different analyses: some oracle-bone forms are read as 行/目/方, while a separate Zhouyuan form is described as 彳/睘. Later bronze and seal forms are analyzed with 辵 and 睘. These descriptions do not establish a continuous change between the forms.

The received dictionary analysis writes 還 as 从辵瞏聲. The graph 还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還 and is used as its simplified form. A separate dictionary entry associates a graph 还 with 不 and other readings, but does not establish a connection to this variant.

uncertainties.text: The connection between the reported early forms and the later 辵/瞏 construction is unclear. The separate 不-associated graph 还 is not established as part of the modern variant’s history.
The received analysis identifies 瞏 as the phonetic element, but the available pronunciation records do not provide a directly comparable historical reconstruction for 瞏 and 還.

senses.text: The received dictionary glosses 還 as 復, “return/repeat,” and cited classical material records the sense “return.” Exact dates for the cited works and artifacts are not given here.

senses.period: bronze and classical attestations; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: 還 is attested with the sense “go around” or “circle.” Its chronological relation to “return” is not established.
A classical citation uses 還 to mean “immediately.” Its relation to “return” or other senses is not established.

senses.period: Tang citations and later uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Adverbial uses include “still” and “yet”; a Tang citation has the sense “still/again.” No dated chain connects these uses to “return.”

senses.period: later cited uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Cited uses include “also,” “more,” and “besides.” Their individual chronology and any path from “return” are not established.

limitations.text: The cited sources document several senses but do not establish a dated sequence or semantic bridges from “return” to “still,” “yet,” “also,” “more,” or “immediately.”

In cited manuscript passages, 還 is proposed as a sound-based spelling for 懷 and 環: the written sign was reused for other words thought to have sounded alike or similarly. The cited material supplies no pronunciation comparisons to demonstrate either match, so these spellings do not show meanings developing from “return.”

overview.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還, whose attested meaning includes “return; go back.” Later 還 combines a movement-related element with a sound element. Modern 还 also means “still” and “yet,” but the sources do not establish a path from “return” to those senses.
